newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ill-fated engagement ring resurfaces from mud.
newsitem.headline: Ill-fated engagement ring resurfaces from mud.

text.p: Margaret Kelleher's engagement ring was stolen by her dog, trampled by cows, starred in an Irish TV game show and unearthed by well-wishers using metal detectors.

The story of Kelleher's ring, told by Thursday's Examiner newspaper, began one weekend in May when the 23-year-old fashion designer took it off and put it in the pocket of her jacket while helping to milk her father's cows.
Her collie dog ran away with the jacket and when she caught up with the animal the ring and other jewellery had vanished somewhere in the mud of her father's farm near Mallow, in southern Ireland.
The family went to church and prayed for the ring's recovery. All summer friends and family scoured the fields around the farm but in vain.
Then Kelleher's mother, Betty, appeared on a tv game show, won herself a holiday in Thailand and told the show's host and audience of her distress at the loss of her daughter's ring.
Last weekend, four days before Kelleher's wedding, two local men rang her and offered to sweep the fields with metal detectors. Kelleher and her fiancee Nicholas Corkery looked on.
The ring was found intact beneath the earth within hours, along with the other jewellery that had been in the jacket.
"There were more tears, but this time they were tears of joy. We got it checked by the jewellers and it was perefect," Betty Kelleher told the newspaper.
